what_its_for: Isotretinoin is used to treat severe acne that has not gotten better with other treatments like antibiotics or skin creams. It works by shrinking the oil glands in your skin, reducing the amount of oil your skin makes, and helping prevent clogged pores. It can dramatically clear up severe, stubborn acne and help prevent scarring.
how_to_take: Take isotretinoin by mouth with a full glass of water. Always take it WITH food or milk — this helps your body absorb the medicine better and reduces stomach upset. Swallow the capsule whole; do not crush, chew, or open it. Take it at the same time every day. IMPORTANT: You must be enrolled in the iPLEDGE program before you can get this medication. You will need to pick up your prescription within 7 days of your doctor visit and fill it within 30 days. Never share this medication with anyone else.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight and how your body responds. The usual dose is 0.5 to 1 milligram per kilogram of body weight per day, often split into two doses. A full course of treatment typically lasts 15 to 20 weeks (about 4 to 5 months). Do not take more or less than your doctor prescribes. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double up to make up for the missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store isotretinoin at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal or take it to a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT get pregnant while taking this medication — it causes very serious birth defects. Two forms of birth control are required during treatment and for 1 month before and after. Do not donate blood during treatment and for 1 month after stopping. Avoid vitamin A supplements, as they can increase side effects. Avoid waxing, laser treatments, dermabrasion, or any skin procedures on treated areas during and for at least 6 months after stopping — your skin will be very sensitive. Avoid excessive sun exposure; always use sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher) and protective clothing. Limit or avoid alcohol, as it may increase certain side effects. Avoid driving at night if your vision in the dark is worse than usual. Do not take tetracycline-type antibiotics (like doxycycline or minocycline) at the same time — this combination can cause dangerous pressure in the brain.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide, depression, or changes in mood or behavior; severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting (could be a sign of pancreatitis); severe headache, blurred vision, or dizziness (signs of increased brain pressure); hearing loss or ringing in the ears; muscle weakness or severe joint or muscle pain; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or very pale stools (liver problems); severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling; chest pain or trouble swallowing; any signs of pregnancy. Also call your doctor if your acne gets much worse or if you develop very dry, cracked, or bleeding lips or skin.
when_it_works: Most people start to see improvement after 1 to 2 months of treatment. Your acne may actually get slightly worse in the first few weeks before it gets better — this is normal. The best results are usually seen after finishing the full course of treatment (4 to 5 months). Some people experience continued improvement for several months after finishing the medication. Many people achieve long-term clearance after just one course of treatment.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Isotretinoin MUST NOT be used during pregnancy. It causes extremely serious birth defects affecting the brain, heart, and face. All patients who could become pregnant must use two forms of birth control, take monthly pregnancy tests, and be enrolled in the iPLEDGE program. BREASTFEEDING: Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. CHILDREN: Not generally recommended for children under 12 years old. Use in teenagers is closely monitored for effects on bone growth and mood. ELDERLY: Use with caution and under close supervision. LIVER or KIDNEY DISEASE: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as dose adjustments may be needed. MENTAL HEALTH: Tell your doctor if you have a history of depression, anxiety, or other mental health conditions, as this medication may worsen these conditions in some patients.
